LESSON: LISTENING 14.1.1 CONSONANT SOUNDS AND INTONATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.1: Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can one learn to correctly pronounce words?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify words with the sounds /v/, /f/, /n/ and /ŋ/ from a text
2. use correct intonation for yes/no and wh- questions in varied contexts
3. appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation and intonation in a conversation

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING 14.1.1 CONSONANT SOUNDS AND INTONATION
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING 14.1.1 CONSONANT SOUNDS AND INTONATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify words with the sounds /v/, /f/, /n/ and /ŋ/ from a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify words with the sounds /v/, /f/, /n/ and /ŋ/ from a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify words with the sounds /v/, /f/, /n/ and /ŋ/ from a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify words with the sounds /v/, /f/, /n/ and /ŋ/ from a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use correct intonation for yes/no and wh- questions in varied contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to use correct intonation for yes/no and wh- questions in varied contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use correct intonation for yes/no and wh- questions in varied contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use correct intonation for yes/no and wh- questions in varied contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation and intonation in a conversation

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation and intonation in a conversation. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation and intonation in a conversation.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation and intonation in a conversation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify words with the sounds /v/, /f/, /n/ and /ŋ/ from a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation to a partner. (skill: use correct intonation for yes/no and wh- questions in varied contexts)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation and intonation in a conversation)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify words with the sounds /v/, /f/, /n/ and /ŋ/ from a text.
3. Practise this skill: use correct intonation for yes/no and wh- questions in varied contexts.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation and intonation in a conversation.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can one learn to correctly pronounce words?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify words with the sounds /v/, /f/, /n/ and /ŋ/ from a text.
5. Be able to: use correct intonation for yes/no and wh- questions in varied contexts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
